label: Copy phase of length-3 sequences (strongest at final output); weak diffuse late-copy firing elsewhere
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), never during original input or on <DEL>, and only on inputs that are repeats (in_first == 0). The strongest, most reliable activations are in L=3 sequences: copy steps there fire 58% of the time, and the final L=3 copy step (recall_idx 2, which outputs the third token) fires 86% of the time and holds about 39% of activation mass. The top examples are all of this form (e.g. a r b <DEL> a [r]). The rest of the mass is spread thinly over the last one or two copy steps (to_go <= 1) of longer sequences, at low rates (2-9%), modulated by token identity (input r, m, l, a raise the rate), and no simple rule captures it. The predicate gets about 46% of mass at precision 0.58; recall is clearly incomplete.
